body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\sum_{k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K}\omega_k E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1]\) for any \(Q\in\mathcal M\) inducing \(P\)
body.estimand_functional: \(\tau_{\omega}(P)=\omega'\theta(P)=E_P[\sum_{k\in\mathcal K}\omega_kR_{k,c_0(k),P}(O)]\).  On the observable equality model this also equals \(E_P[b(X)'R_P(O)]\) for every integrable feasible loading satisfying \(A'b(X)=\omega\).  The loading \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance only within this aggregate pairwise-score family.  At conditional-mean interior laws with fixed finite covariate support, published-model efficiency is determined by projecting \(\psi_P^0\) onto \(\mathcal T_{P,\mathrm{OVS}}\), yielding \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is canonical only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero.  No continuous-covariate canonical-gradient claim is made.

sampling_model.design: Observational staggered adoption in a balanced fixed-\(T\) panel under the literal global OVS period-by-period covariate-conditional DDD restrictions, using every cohort clean at each period.
sampling_model.units: \((O_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independent and identically distributed panel units.
sampling_model.treatment: Enabling is absorbing through cohort \(G\), and effective treatment requires \(S=1\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every cohort--eligibility cell entering a retained clean comparison has conditional probability at least \(\varepsilon\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For the proved attainment and efficiency-gap inference regimes, \(X\) has fixed finite support with masses bounded below.  Cell averages estimate every retained propensity, regression, shared-cell second cross-moment, and published normal moment.  The target estimator uses fixed-fold orthogonal OVS signals and \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\), \(0<a<1/4\).  The gap estimator is the explicit rank-thresholded plug-in \(F_{z,\tau_n}(\widehat\mu)\), with absolute-eigenvalue thresholding for indefinite comparator KKT systems.

body.tldr: For the published global OVS staggered-DDD model, this note proves the full-data/observed-law image for arbitrary covariate support.  At fixed finite-support covariate laws it exhausts the observed tangent normal generated by every period-admissible clean cohort and derives the canonical gradient \(\phi_{\mathrm{OVS},P}=\psi_P^0-r_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)'K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)^\dagger Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\).  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) remains only the optimum inside the aggregate pairwise-score family and is canonical exactly when its published-normal equation holds.  A fixed-support cross-fitted estimator attains \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), and a finite-support moment map gives pointwise Wald inference for comparator efficiency gaps away from equality and rank changes.  In the corrected bounded binary witness, the best joint constant loading loses exactly \(3/512\) and the published componentwise OVS loading loses \(15/512\), both relative to the published bound.

project_justification.gap: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna establish staggered-DDD identification, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise weighting, and a two-period DDD efficient influence function, while Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami derive a nonparametric two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function.  These results do not provide the fixed-finite-support observed tangent exhaustion for the overidentified global staggered OVS restriction system or pointwise inference for the resulting published-bound comparator gap.
project_justification.niche: The global OVS model contains period-specific eligibility-gap normal directions beyond terminal clean-comparison contrasts.  At fixed finite-support covariate laws, an explicit affine-support right inverse and bounded likelihood tilts exhaust those directions.  The resulting canonical object is the projection of a reference gradient onto the published tangent space, including singular normal operators and shared-cell covariances; the conditional loading \(b^\star(X)\) solves a distinct restricted score-family problem.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 is used only as a conditional-precision architectural comparator, and no nesting relation is asserted.
project_justification.fill: The note proves the general observed-law/full-data equivalence, proves fixed-finite-support published tangent exhaustion by an exact dominated-tilt construction, derives the singular Moore--Penrose canonical projection, and gives an attaining fixed-support cross-fitted estimator.  It also supplies an exact two-period panel-DDD reduction, a finite-moment map with pointwise Wald inference for the published-bound comparator gap, and a corrected bounded witness whose best joint constant and componentwise OVS losses are \(3/512\) and \(15/512\), respectively.

body.related_work: Ortiz--Villavicencio and Sant'Anna provide the staggered-DDD identifying architecture, pairwise-score limit theory, constant componentwise benchmark, and, in Supplemental Appendix Lemma A.2, a two-period panel-DDD efficient influence function.  Akbari, Kiyavash, and Ghassami's Theorem 5 gives the corresponding nonparametric four-cell panel-DDD efficient influence function; Proposition \(\ref{prop:two-period-eif-reduction}\) gives the note's term-by-term singleton-comparison reduction, including the target-share derivative.  Chen, Sant'Anna, and Xie's Theorem 3.2 supplies a normalized conditional-precision efficient influence-function formula for its staggered-DiD target; it is retained only as an architectural comparator, and no equivalence or nesting of tangent spaces is claimed.  Newey supplies the cited generalized-inverse conditional-moment geometry, Chernozhukov and coauthors supply the cross-fitting template used by the attainment result, Hsieh supplies the shared-comparison fixed-weight limit-law comparator, and Borusyak, Jaravel, and Spiess delimit the distinct efficient-imputation route.  The contribution here is general observable/full-data equivalence together with fixed-finite-support OVS tangent exhaustion, canonical projection, attainment, and pointwise comparator-gap inference.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The observed-law/full-data equivalence allows arbitrary covariate support, but tangent exhaustion and canonicality are proved only at conditional-mean interior laws with fixed finite covariate support.  The proof uses a finite collection of affine-support right inverses; no measurable uniformly bounded analogue is established for continuously distributed covariates.  Target attainment and comparator-gap inference are likewise fixed-support and pointwise.  Gap inference assumes positive influence variance and separation from equality by \(\delta_0>0\) and is not uniform across comparator or normal-rank changes.  The external efficient-influence-function equivalence is confined to the two-period, two-cohort, singleton-comparison panel-DDD specialization.  No nesting with the distinct staggered-DiD tangent system, growing-sieve continuous-covariate theorem, or uniform confidence procedure under weak or changing positive eigenvalues of \(K_{\mathrm{OVS},P}(X)\) is proved.
body.honest_scope: The note covers a fixed finite horizon and target set.  Its observable/full-data characterization is general in the covariate distribution, whereas its tangent-space, canonical-gradient, attainment, and comparator-gap inference results require fixed finite covariate support and are pointwise at conditional-mean interior laws.  It distinguishes the published bound \(V_{\mathrm{OVS}}\), the localized bound \(V_{\mathrm{can}}\), and the aggregate score-family variance \(V_{\mathrm{agg}}\); \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P\) is not presented as canonical without its published-normal equation.  In the bounded witness, all normal closures coincide, so \(3/512\) is the minimum published-bound loss over deterministic feasible loadings and \(15/512\) is the componentwise OVS loss at \(r=\omega_2=1/2\).  The two-period influence-function comparison is an exact special-case reduction.  A CRAN \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend is proposed only as future work.  No continuous-covariate canonicality or Wald theorem, equality-boundary inference, staggered-DiD tangent-space nesting, or rank-uniform guarantee is claimed.
body.interpretation: At a fixed finite-support covariate law there are three precision frontiers.  Conditional loading by \(b^\star(X)\) minimizes variance within the aggregate pairwise-score family.  Projection against \(Z_P^{\mathrm{per}}\) gives the larger localized model's bound, while projection against the exhaustively justified \(Z_P^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) gives the published model's canonical gradient and smaller bound.  A loaded pairwise score is therefore called semiparametrically efficient only when its published-normal conditional moment is zero.  The corrected witness makes the normal closures coincide but separates the comparators: the best deterministic loading loses \(3/512\) at the benchmark and the componentwise OVS rule loses \(15/512\).  Integration of the certified fixed-support estimator, diagnostics, and pointwise gap interval as an optional CRAN \(\texttt{triplediff}\) backend is future work, not an implemented contribution of this note.
